named_confounds: genre composition shift (late period dominated by juvenile works)
sparse early-period cells (e.g. romance n=40, collection n=37)

one passage per work so rates are binary and noisy
rationale: Methods: 6766 works, one annotated passage each; rate = count__domains__DISTANCE_TRAVEL / n_passages. Early = year<1876, late = year>=1876. Within each of 8 genres, works averaged with equal weight per period; late-minus-early differences averaged with equal genre weight. 95% CI from 2000 bootstrap resamples of works stratified by genre x period. Result: +0.025 passage-rate units, CI [0.004, 0.045]. 6 of 8 genres increase (adventure and sensation_mystery decrease slightly). Decade means rise from ~0.03-0.07 pre-1850 to ~0.11-0.12 after 1890. Sensitivity: the effect stays positive within high (0.015), medium (0.022) and low (0.043) date-confidence subsets, within UK, US and unknown origin, and in a narrow 1850-1899 window (0.018). Caveats: the early period is thin (about 750 works vs 6000 late), and some genre cells are tiny. Romance (0/40 early) and collection contribute a large share of the effect. Point estimates are weaker for well-dated works, and the CI lower bound is close to zero. Alternative explanations include changes in corpus sampling or genre makeup, and labeling drift. The cited passages are travel-tagged passages from late works. They show the construct but cannot establish the trend on their own. Overall: a modest increase, supported with moderate confidence.
